description: Increased risk of bleeding due to combined anticoagulant and antiplatelet effects.
NSAIDs increase bleeding risk when combined with warfarin.
Risk of lactic acidosis, especially with renal impairment.
Increased risk of statin-induced myopathy and rhabdomyolysis.
Risk of hyperkalemia when ACE inhibitors are combined with potassium supplements.
Increased risk of serotonin syndrome.
Increased risk of lactic acidosis and hypoglycemia.
Increased simvastatin plasma concentration, raising myopathy risk at higher doses.
Reduces antiplatelet effectiveness of clopidogrel via CYP2C19 inhibition.
Diuretic-induced hypokalemia increases risk of digoxin toxicity.
Increased theophylline levels, risk of seizures and arrhythmia.
May potentiate anticoagulant effect, increasing bleeding risk.
High-dose or prolonged use may mildly potentiate anticoagulant effect.
Combined negative chronotropic/inotropic effect, risk of bradycardia and heart block.
Combined glucose-lowering effect; monitor for hypoglycemia, generally safe combination.
Increased statin levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, raising myopathy risk.
Risk of hyperkalemia with combined ARB and potassium-sparing diuretic.
Fluconazole increases phenytoin levels, risk of toxicity.
NSAIDs reduce methotrexate clearance, increasing toxicity risk.
Calcium reduces levothyroxine absorption; space doses by 4 hours.
